messages:
michelle (devex): quick sync — we need to lock API surface for next small release. two customer asks: 1) typed structured-output helpers in both python/ts, 2) an embeddings merge primitive for streaming use-cases. which to prioritize?

jordan (sdk): +1 on structured-output types, customers keep sending validation errors. small SDK surface but heavy docs/examples work.

elyse (pm): customer A (fintech) will only go to prod if structured-output types land. customer B (ads) needs embeddings-merge for cheap rerank pipelines. both are paid.

sam (eng-runtime): embeddings-merge only needs a lightweight server-side op: `POST /v1/embeddings/merge` that concatenates vectors and returns meta. latency impact negligible. runtime can ship a compat shim.

michelle (devex): ok, what about ergonomics? jordan, do you foresee breaking changes?

jordan (sdk): for structured-output we can add `types.StructuredSchema` and helper `client.parse_structured(response, schema)` in patch release. no breaking change. examples will need updated sample prompts.

chris (docs): examples effort estimate: structured-output — 3 short guides (py/ts + migration); embeddings-merge — 1 guide + small Runner example. docs time similar, but structured-output requires eval checklist.

tariq (product): launch criteria suggestion:
- structured-output: type definitions in both SDKs, 3 canonical examples, eval harness for 2 customer prompts, docs + changelog entry.
- embeddings-merge: SDK convenience fn, server shim deployed, one production customer signoff, perf smoke tests.

michelle (devex): schedule-wise? we have the sprint window — 2 weeks. can we do both as smaller slices? propose we do structured-output first (higher adoption risk) and land embeddings-merge as a follow-up patch.

jordan (sdk): agree. plan: week1 — types + parse helper + py/ts examples; week2 — docs polish, changelog, and cut release. embeddings-merge in sprint+1 with runtime shim ready now.

sam (eng-runtime): I'll drop the shim PR today and add smoke tests. tagging @deploy-bot for canary once merged.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: `canary-embed-merge-19512346` on us-west-2 in 3h.

elyse (pm): risk tradeoff: if structured-output exposes subtle behavioral regressions, we need quick rollback path in SDK — versioned helpers?

jordan (sdk): we'll feature-flag the parse helper behind `Client.flags.structured_parsing = true` and default to off for initial release. that gives us fast rollback. no breaking change.

michelle (devex): good. docs actions: chris — start the structured-output spec doc (include minimal typed examples + failure modes). jordan — add code comments + sample prompt templates. elyse/tariq — get the customer A eval prompts by EOD. sam — runtime shim PR link in thread.

chris (docs): noted. I'll use the internal template: https://redwood.internal/docs/templates/sdk-example.md and draft the eval checklist.

sam (eng-runtime): PR: https://phabricator.redwood/r/12345 — includes merge endpoint + smoke tests.

michelle (devex): final call: landing order = 1) structured-output gated release, 2) embeddings-merge follow-up. owners: jordan (sdk) + chris (docs) + sam (runtime) + elyse (pm).

jordan (sdk): putting up a lightweight RFC in repo under `devex/sdk/rfcs/structured-output-1951234567.md` now.

michelle (devex): thanks all — will post a short announcement once the gated release is cut. :tada:

michelle (devex): THREAD END
